tasks.short: Read the exam programme and school requirements, write the course outline and objectives, build the period schedule, agree the outline with the section, and publish it to students.

steps.what: Technical teacher reads the exam programme and school requirements
Technical teacher prepares objectives and outlines for courses of study following curriculum guidelines

loop.input: The exam programme, the school's requirements and last year's outline.
loop.output: A draft course outline with weekly topics and objectives.
loop.check: Code checks every exam programme code in scope is covered and each objective links to a code; the teacher edits and approves the outline.
loop.stop: Stops when the checks pass and the teacher approves, or after two failed redrafts the teacher writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Weekly topics and objectives need prose for each course; the code list alone is not an outline.

steps.what: Technical teacher builds the period schedule in a spreadsheet
Technical teacher agrees the outline and schedule with the section
Technical teacher uploads the outline for students

tasks.design: A bounded step drafts the course outline from the exam programme, the school's requirements and last year's outline; code checks coverage of every exam programme code, and the teacher edits. The period schedule is laid out by code over the school's teaching weeks and holidays. Once the section has agreed, the outline is published in the learning environment ({LMS}). Reading the requirements and agreeing with the section stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Outlines were rewritten each year and schedules built by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models draft outlines; code lays schedules over a calendar.
tasks.still_hard: A good outline reflects what went wrong last year, which no file holds.
tasks.human_edge: Ordering topics so students see a real job early.
tasks.altitude: The teacher edits outlines and checks coverage instead of writing from scratch.

reach.learn: Whether coverage gaps show before the year starts.

evidence.claim: With Oak's Aila, 464 primary teachers cut weekly preparation from 3.3 to 2.5 hours with quality no worse, though use declined over ten weeks.
Drafting course outlines is not an Annex III use; AI that evaluates learning outcomes is.

assumptions: Boundary: from the exam programme to the outline published; the testing plan is outside.
Input contract: exam programme from the national body; school calendar from the timetabling office; fallback is writing by hand.
Agreeing with the section does not change.
No student data go into the drafting step.
research_questions: How much of the drafted outline survives the teacher's edit?

already_counted.description: Technical teacher edits and approves the drafted outline.

incremental.description: Technical teacher keeps the school calendar data current.

approvals.approved_version: The outline and schedule text as agreed with the section in s4, published unchanged for the students of that course; any later edit needs agreement again.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: new courses; high: repeat courses with yearly updates.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare a progress overview, set up talk slots, have parents choose a slot, meet parents to discuss progress, priorities and resource needs, record them, and pass needs to the care coordinator.

steps.what: Technical teacher prepares a progress overview for each student
Technical teacher sets up talk slots on paper lists and by e-mail
Parents choose a talk slot
Technical teacher meets with parents to discuss their children's progress and to determine priorities and resource needs
Technical teacher records priorities and resource needs in the student record
Technical teacher passes resource needs to the care coordinator

tasks.design: The student system ({OTHER}) prints a one-page progress overview per student with results, absence and earlier agreements, so the teacher does not compile it. Parents choose a talk slot in the school's parent app. Priorities and resource needs go into a short template in the record. The talk with parents and passing needs to the care coordinator stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Overviews were compiled by hand and talk slots arranged on paper lists and by e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Student systems print progress overviews; parent apps offer slot choice.
tasks.still_hard: Ten-minute talks leave little room for real problems.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing what parents need for their child beyond grades.

reach.task: Plan a talk about their child

evidence.claim: Student systems can print progress overviews; parent apps offer slot choice.
Under the WMS, parents and pupils consent to rules on pupil data.

assumptions: Boundary: from student results to needs passed on; arranging extra support is outside.
Input contract: results from the student system; slots opened in the parent app; fallback is paper lists and e-mail.
Parents choose a slot in the app in about the time an e-mail reply took; priced as customer time.
The talk with parents does not change.

incremental.description: Technical teacher opens talk slots in the parent app.
Parents choose a talk slot in the parent app.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few talks and parents who prefer paper; high: report evenings with many talks.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Talk with students about placement wishes, search for companies, match students to placements, send applications, prepare the placement agreement, send it for signature, and refer students to placement services.

steps.what: Technical teacher talks with students about placement and job wishes
Technical teacher searches for placement companies by phone and e-mail
Technical teacher places students in jobs by matching them to placements and checks the student's application for that company
Technical teacher e-mails the student's application to the company
Technical teacher prepares the placement agreement
Technical teacher sends the agreement to the company, student and parents for signature
Technical teacher makes referrals to job placement services

tasks.design: Accredited placement companies are searchable by trade and distance in the school's placement database ({OTHER}), so fewer calls are needed. Once the teacher has matched a student, the application goes from the database to the company. The placement agreement is generated from student and company data; once the teacher has checked it, it goes out for electronic signature ({ESIGN}) by company, student and parents. Talking with students, matching and referring to placement services stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Companies were found by phone and agreements filled in and posted on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Placement databases list accredited companies; agreements can be generated and signed electronically.
tasks.still_hard: Good companies for weaker students are scarce.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which company owner will give a shy student a chance.

reach.learn: Whether agreements come back signed sooner.

evidence.claim: Placement databases can list companies by trade and distance; agreements can be generated from records and signed electronically.
Sharing a student's application with a company is processing of personal data and needs a basis under the GDPR.

assumptions: Boundary: from the student's wishes to questions settled; supervising the placement is outside.
Input contract: company data from the placement database; student data from the student system; fallback is phone and paper.
Matching and referring stay with the teacher.
Companies, students and parents sign electronically in about the time paper took.
research_questions: Do placements start on time more often?

approvals.approved_version: The student's application (CV and letter) as checked by the teacher in s3, addressed to the matched placement company; a different company or changed documents need a new check before sending.

The placement agreement text with company, student, dates and conditions as checked by the teacher in s5, sent for signature to the company, student and parents named in it; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few placements with known companies; high: many placements each year.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select equipment and materials, write and place the order, receive and store deliveries, issue tools and materials to students, and take inventory.

steps.what: Technical teacher selects equipment, materials and supplies for the coming period
Technical teacher writes the order list
Technical teacher checks and approves the final order list: items, quantities and delivery date
Technical teacher orders classroom supplies from the supplier
Technical teacher receives deliveries and stores them in the store room
Technical teacher checks deliveries against the order and records receipt
Technical teacher issues tools and materials to students
Technical teacher records which tools and materials went to which student
Technical teacher counts classroom equipment and supplies for the inventory
Technical teacher reconciles the count with the stock list and records differences

tasks.design: Materials are ordered from the school's purchasing catalogue ({PROCUREMENT}) with framework suppliers, so the list is picked from catalogue lines instead of typed from supplier sites; after the teacher checks the final list, the catalogue sends that version to the supplier. Receiving, storing, issuing and counting stay physical and keep their time. Only the records change: deliveries are ticked off against the order on a tablet instead of a paper delivery note, issues are scanned against the student's card instead of written on a list, and the count is reconciled against a stock list that the scans keep current instead of a spreadsheet rebuilt each period.
tasks.previous_blocker: Orders were e-mailed, issues written on paper and counts reconciled in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: School purchasing catalogues and barcode issue lists are easy to set up.
tasks.still_hard: Students lose or break tools without scanning them back.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing material that is cheap enough to waste while learning.

evidence.claim: Purchasing catalogues send orders to framework suppliers; barcode issue lists keep stock current.

assumptions: Boundary: from the course outline to the inventory; paying invoices is outside.
Input contract for s2 and s4: catalogue kept by the school's purchasing team; items outside the catalogue are ordered by e-mail as today.
Input contract for s8 and s10: student cards with barcodes and labelled tools.
Receiving, storing, issuing and counting keep their full time; only the record steps s6, s8 and s10 are priced, at what the tablet and scans remove.
research_questions: Do stock differences at period end fall?

incremental.description: Technical teacher follows up unreturned tools.

approvals.approved_version: The order list with items, quantities and delivery date as checked by the teacher in s3; any change needs a new check before the order goes out.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few catalogue items and little issuing; high: a large workshop with many items issued.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The technical teacher keeps choosing what to teach, meeting parents, matching students to placements and selecting materials; rewritten outlines, paper lists, phone searches and full stock counts shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A teacher who spends saved time building ties with local employers.
